DECISION: ACCEPT the chunks_embedding HNSW index as shipped, with a documented caveat. No production default changed (hnsw.iterative_scan stays off).

Measured with real EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of the production query (single repo/branch, ANALYZE before every EXPLAIN, pgvector default m=16/ef_construction=64/ef_search=40), scaling 100 to 50,000 chunks:

  100/250/500/750 rows: Seq Scan + Sort (unforced)
  1,000-15,000 rows:    Index Scan chunks_embedding (unforced) -- crossover measured between 750 and 1,000
  17,500/20,000 rows:   Seq Scan + Sort again -- CAVEAT, ~40x slower (1.1-2.3ms -> 42-52ms), silent
  25,000-50,000 rows:   Index Scan chunks_embedding (unforced) again

The crossover to HNSW (750->1,000) is clean and holds through 50k except for the 17.5k-20k band. Verified the band is NOT: an incremental-seeding artifact (reproduces on a fresh, directly-seeded container), stale stats/autovacuum interference (autovacuum disabled, ANALYZE confirmed effective via pg_stat_user_tables: analyze_count=1, n_mod_since_analyze=0), or HNSW build/maintenance lag (survives REINDEX). Likely mechanism identified by reading pgvector's cost-estimator source (src/hnsw.c hnswcostestimate's TOAST/page-count discount branch, sensitive to chunks.embedding being TOASTed out of the main heap) but not confirmed via server-side instrumentation -- tracked as follow-up loam-l73.

Also corrected: internal/chunkstore/integration_test.go had a stale comment claiming "Seq Scan" and "no btree on (repo_id, target_branch)" for its 3-row fixture -- both wrong (the btree exists, 0002:92, and is what a never-ANALYZE-d tiny table picks; verified live that adding ANALYZE flips the identical table to Seq Scan). internal/storesuite/hnsw_integration_test.go's narration updated so it does not imply the index is reluctant in production -- confirmed via grep that package's chunks table only ever holds this one test's 3 rows (not a multi-repo selectivity effect), so the real cause there is the same missing ANALYZE, not fixture-shared-container selectivity as initially hypothesized.

Fixed by loam-ofg.21. The bind-close-rebind window is gone entirely: the harness keeps its *net.TCPListener open, dups it via .File(), and passes it to the child through os/exec ExtraFiles (fd 3), which newListener wraps with net.FileListener when LOAM_LISTENER_FD is set. The port is never unbound, so there is no window to lose. Review also caught that net.FileListener DUPS -- the source *os.File was never closed, so fd 3 leaked for the child's lifetime and the socket stayed in LISTEN even after Shutdown closed the listener, meaning 'stop accepting connections' was not actually achieved in fd mode. Fixed with defer file.Close(), verified by a test confirmed to fail against the old code with 'address already in use'. Side effect: the old TCP-dial readiness check had to become an HTTP poll, because with FD-passing a bare dial completes into the backlog the instant the HARNESS binds, before the child exists -- the old check would have returned immediately and raced every startup.

ROOT CAUSE: a double-owned file descriptor, not environmental contention (that theory was ruled out by reproducing on a quiet machine at load 2.85 with zero sibling agents). cmd/server/serve_test.go handed newListener the same fd number its own *os.File held, giving two Go values ownership of one descriptor. newListener closed its copy deterministically -- correct, that is loam-2m0's fd-leak fix and it was deliberately left untouched -- while the test's *os.File kept an ARMED FINALIZER that closed the same number again whenever GC ran, by which point the OS had reassigned it to an unrelated live socket in the same test binary. That is why the symptoms were impossible for a timing bug: 'dial tcp: bad file descriptor', EOF mid-request, and 'malformed HTTP status code "/loam.v1.RepoService/GetRepo"' (one client reading another's REQUEST line), all unaffected by -parallel=1 and -race. Fixed test-side with syscall.Dup so each side owns exactly one descriptor. Production is unaffected -- there the fd crosses a process boundary via ExtraFiles. Added TestOSFileDoubleClose_ClobbersReusedDescriptor, a DETERMINISTIC reproduction using runtime.SetFinalizer plus a channel barrier and POSIX lowest-fd reuse, rather than a probabilistic guard. Audited every .File()/os.NewFile/syscall.Dup/.Fd() site: main_integration_test.go's startServer verified safe (single owner, closed once immediately after cmd.Start()). Verified 30/30 clean on cmd/server plus 3 consecutive full -race sweeps. Drain test tightened from 30s to 5s against a measured ~200-300ms actual.

Reviewed PASS. Two-layer validate-then-verify: an allowlist requiring every /-delimited segment to match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$, so '.', '..' and empty segments are impossible BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by blacklisting known-bad strings, plus filepath.IsLocal on the composed path (the only layer guarding the third joined segment, agentIdentifier, which the allowlist never sees). Invalid input ERRORS with exit 2; it does not sanitize, so an attempt is never silently rewritten into a colliding path. Reviewer probed 30 adversarial inputs -- including NFC/NFD 'cafe', U+2044 fraction slash, U+FF0F fullwidth solidus, U+202E RTL override, '....//....//', NUL bytes, and shell metacharacters -- all rejected; no non-ASCII byte can reach the filesystem, making APFS normalization moot by construction. Six mutations run: all four security-weakening ones died; the two survivors were strictly benign (a redundant empty-string fast path, and > vs >= on the length bound, which is stricter not weaker). Trailing dots probed on real APFS: 'a.' and 'a' stay distinct, no hazard on darwin or linux. Trust boundary independently verified -- only cmd/loam imports internal/cli, so nothing server-side can reach StagingPath, making this a local-invocation defense rather than the remote path the Loam-Agent-* headers represent. Follow-ups filed: loam-e9u (a DEMONSTRATED symlink bypass -- filepath.IsLocal is purely lexical, so a pre-planted symlink lets a fully-valid key write outside the workspace; belongs to the first writer, loam-0pj.12, and now blocks it) and loam-5j5 (corrected: IsLocal bounds the path but not its DEPTH, so a malformed agentIdentifier cannot escape but CAN collapse onto the staging root and destroy per-agent isolation). Merged in main.

KEY SEMANTIC FINDING, now recorded on loam-ofg.10: graph refs needs a TWO-STEP composition. LookupSymbolsByName's empty result IS authoritative not-found; LookupReferencesByName's is NOT, because a real symbol can have zero references and symbol_references carries no symbol_id to join through. Review found an UNRECOVERABLE dead-end reachable WITHOUT a crash: RequestReview committed UpdateState then opened the round as a separate call, and connect-go cancels the request context on client disconnect or deadline, so an ordinary CLI Ctrl-C or timeout between two round-trips sufficed. The resulting reviewable-with-no-round branch was visible AND broken -- the awaiting-verdict filter's NOT EXISTS is TRUE when no rounds exist, so it appeared in every reviewer's queue and then rejected every verdict via errNoCurrentRound. It was unrecoverable because UpdateState's guard has no reviewable->reviewable edge, so a retry returned ErrIllegalTransition before ever reaching OpenRound; and the error inverted, reporting 'failed precondition' which reads as 'you forgot a title'.

Fixed with an idempotent self-heal rather than full atomicity: on ErrIllegalTransition from an already-reviewable branch, check CurrentRound and open one if genuinely missing. Verified bounded in BOTH directions -- I mutated it to over-trigger (heal even when a round exists) and TestRequestReview_AlreadyReviewableWithRound_ReturnsFailedPrecondition caught it, so it cannot mask a legitimate rejection. Exported reviewstore.ErrNoCurrentRound for the check.

Review also found 7 surviving mutations across the list/paging/enum surface (Target and Author filters, Page.offset, defaultListLimit, explicit UNSPECIFIED state, three enum round-trips, cross-repo name resolution) -- all now covered. ROOT CAUSE: macOS Command Line Tools ship a SYSTEM gitconfig (/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/share/git-core/gitconfig) setting credential.helper=osxkeychain, and the test helpers passed os.Environ() straight through, so the client git used it. osxkeychain keys entries by protocol+host and IGNORES THE PORT. Every fakeforge server binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and most register the same token string ('push-token'), so once any authenticating test stored a credential for 127.0.0.1, the helper handed that same token to TestGitCloneFailsWithoutCredentials -- which supplies none deliberately -- and the server, genuinely holding that token, accepted it. The unauthenticated clone succeeded and the guard inverted.

Not load, and not the fakeforge instances colliding as first suspected. The stray 'CGI error: chdir ...: no such file or directory' lines were the SAME cause: those requests only reached the CGI backend because they had been wrongly authenticated first, so they vanish with the fix.

Ruled out along the way: a global credential.helper (unset), the mux routing (only /git/ serves git, and it is auth-gated), and hasToken (mutex-guarded). Confirmed git clone against a 401 always exits 128 with 'fatal: Authentication failed', which proved the server must have authorised the request rather than the test misreading an error.

FIX: scrub the client git environment instead of inheriting it -- GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 drops the system file, HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME point at a per-test temp dir, and credential.helper is explicitly cleared with -c per invocation.

VERIFIED BY A/B under -race -count=25 -parallel 16: isolation removed -> TestGitCloneFailsWithoutCredentials FAILS and 25 CGI errors appear; isolation in place -> zero of both, across repeated runs. Full integration sweep green (35 packages). Merged in main.

MACHINE-DEPENDENT: this only fires where a keychain-style credential helper is configured, which is why it showed locally on macOS and not in ubuntu CI -- and why it was dismissed twice as load.

Credentials store over token-only AES-GCM. Encryption layering verified correct: all nonce generation lives in internal/crypto (fresh rand per call, version||nonce||sealed), so the store has no nonce logic to get wrong -- a fixed-nonce mutation fails crypto's own tests and correctly does not touch this package. Raw-column-never-plaintext, wrong-key-fails-cleanly, and round-trip all exercise a live row. No token or key is ever formatted into an error or log line.

Status projection is structurally leak-proof: GetCredentialStatusRow/ListCredentialStatusesRow have NO ciphertext field, so a status-only caller cannot be handed the token even by accident -- proven by passing a Decrypt-panics encryptor through GetStatus/ListStatuses. errNotFound vs errNoToken genuinely distinguish 'never enrolled' from 'enrolled, not yet credentialed'. 12 mutations run; the only survivors were equivalent mutants.

ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: the upsert left validated at its previous value when a token was REPLACED, so after SetValidated(host,true) a later UpsertToken reported validated:true for a token nothing had checked -- and a caller whose re-validation errored before writing SetValidated(false) would inherit the old verdict. The flag describes one token, not the host; this is the same drift GetCredentialStatus avoids for has_token by computing it. Adding validated=false passed the ENTIRE existing suite in both directions, so the semantics was unspecified and untested either way. Added a regression test verified to FAIL without the clause.

Pre-receive policy socket, hook binary, and ref-policy evaluation. Reviewed FIXES-REQUIRED then fixed and re-verified.

END-TO-END PROOF with real git, real compiled hook, real socket, real ReconcileMirror -- all four spec rules rejecting with reasons visible to the client:
  remote: loam: refs/heads/main is read-only (target branch)
  remote: loam: refs/heads/wb-never-registered is not a work branch; create one with 'work start'
  remote: loam: wb-owned-by-bob belongs to bob
  remote: loam: wb-closed is closed
plus an allowed push landing on the mirror, and fail-closed when the socket is absent.

MUST-FIX 1, and it inverted my own read of the risk: the os.Chdir bind fallback did not merely MASK a config problem, it created a silent permanent outage. connect(2) is subject to the same sun_path limit as bind(2), and cmd/loamhook builds the absolute path with no chdir of its own -- so in exactly the deployment where the fallback engaged, the server reported a HEALTHY startup and rejected 100% of pushes forever with an opaque message. The test that 'verified' the fallback never dialled the socket it bound. Fallback deleted; bind now fails loudly naming the limit and telling the operator to shorten LOAM_DATA_DIR. A second hazard went with it: the relative bind made Close() unlink relative to the RESTORED cwd, deleting a decoy ./hook.sock and leaving the real socket behind.

MUST-FIX 2: a fail-open mutation survived the whole suite -- 'len(resp.Verdicts) == 0 -> return 0' accepts every push whenever the response carries no verdicts, which is EXACTLY what the server returns on a hard evaluation error, i.e. when Postgres is down. Now guarded, and the agent additionally gets a loam:-prefixed explanation instead of silence on that path. I re-applied the mutant myself after the fix and confirmed it dies.

Also fixed: isTerminal is now an allowlist (a future sixth state would previously have been allowed to push), empty agentName rejected explicitly, loamhook binary stat'd at startup so a fresh install cannot boot without it, and two mutation survivors covered (break-after-first-reason, verdictless rejection).

Design calls upheld: a compiled Go hook rather than /bin/sh, correct because ofg.16 builds the receive-pack environment explicitly and nothing guarantees curl or nc; hook derives the socket path from its cwd, which git guarantees is the bare repo; the binary is copied atomically via temp+chmod+rename, which also avoids ETXTBSY when replacing a hook mid-exec, and stale detection is inherent since it rewrites wholesale. PostAcceptFunc fires only on full acceptance, reuses the already-fetched row for loam-giq.6, and cannot flip a verdict. All four reason strings byte-exact against docs/git-spec.md:148-151, with honest in-code disclaimers where a rule generalizes beyond spec text.

MERGE INTERACTION worth recording: removing the fallback made the sun_path limit real, which immediately failed clonepush_integration_test.go (landed on main after this branched, still using t.TempDir()). Fixed by pointing it at the same short-data-dir helper. That is the fallback removal working as intended -- the failure now surfaces at the misconfiguration instead of becoming an undialable socket.
